title: Mandi – Spiced Rice with Meat
description: Mandi is a traditional Yemeni Arabic dish made with fragrant basmati rice and tender slow-cooked chicken or lamb, infused with aromatic spices and finished with a signature charcoal-smoked aroma. It is a celebratory dish known for its depth of flavor and restaurant-style presentation.

ingredients.title: For the Meat (Chicken or Lamb)
items: 1.5–2 kg whole chicken (cut into halves/quarters) or lamb shoulder/leg (bone-in, large pieces)
1 dried lime (loomi), pierced with a fork (optional)

ingredients.title: For the Mandi Spice Mix (Hawaij al-Mandi)
For the Rice
items: 4 cups meat stock (from cooking the meat)
½ tsp saffron threads soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk (for garnish & aroma)
½ cup raisins (optional, lightly fried in ghee)
½ cup almonds or cashews (fried in ghee, for garnish)

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Prepare the Meat:
• Rub chicken or lamb with 2 tbsp spice mix and salt. Marinate at least 1 hour.
• Heat ghee in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, and tomatoes until golden.
• Add whole spices, dried lime, and meat. Sear until browned.
• Add water, bring to boil, skim impurities, then simmer until tender (45 min chicken, ~2 hrs lamb).
• Remove meat and reserve strained stock.

2. Cook the Rice:
• Heat ghee in a wide pot and sauté onions until golden.
• Add garlic, whole spices, and soaked rice. Stir gently.
• Pour in hot stock, add 1 tbsp spice mix, and salt.
• Cover and cook on low heat for 15–20 minutes until fluffy.

3. Final Smoking (Dum Technique):
• Place cooked meat over rice.
• Heat charcoal until red hot and place in a small foil cup on rice.
• Drizzle ghee over charcoal and immediately cover tightly.
• Let smoke infuse for 10–15 minutes.

4. Garnish & Serve:
• Fluff rice gently and arrange meat on top.
• Drizzle saffron milk.
• Garnish with fried nuts and raisins.
• Serve hot with tomato chutney or yogurt.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Pair with yogurt or cucumber raita
Serve as a centerpiece dish for gatherings

chefTips: Use aged basmati rice for best fluffy texture.
Lamb shoulder adds richer, deeper flavor than lean cuts.
Charcoal smoking (dum) is essential for authentic restaurant aroma.
Do not over-stir rice to maintain grain separation.
Ghee enhances aroma and traditional authenticity.
